jobs.prompt: Item C: setting a ticket status by hand needs a guard. From an investigation: runTicketsCommand in tools/scope-commands.mjs (around lines 1716 to 1733) handles --set without confirmation, parseArgs already accepts --force, --yes and --dry-run booleans but the handler ignores them, and --dry-run still takes the lock and writes. Fix: validate and preview the requested transition (show ID, from, to); with --dry-run return before any lock, write, plan refresh or log; otherwise require --force or --yes, and without either print the preview and refuse with a clear message that names the flag; --force only bypasses the confirmation, never transition legality, unapproved proposals or unmet dependencies; update SCOPE_USAGE. In tools/tickets.mjs extend transition options and its log event with actor, source and confirmation fields (actor from the OS user name or SWARM_ACTOR, source tickets-set), keeping by owner for compatibility; the log line stays one JSON object per line. Tests in tests/scope-set-guard.test.mjs: bare --set refuses with no writes (ledger and log unchanged); --force and --yes apply one legal transition with actor metadata in the log; --dry-run with and without --force changes nothing (no ledger, log, plan, lock); an illegal transition, an invalid id or status and an unapproved proposal are refused even with --force. ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENT (atlas-seafloor: tickets --set done on sensitive tickets bypassed the required Opus security review for 14 tickets): setting a ticket to done by hand must never skip the review gate. In the --set handler, when the target status is done and the ticket requires a security review or an acceptance review (use the same decision cmdSync uses for sensitive tickets, securityReviewReason, and the acceptance requirement from the project profile) and no passing review for it is recorded in the ticket's evidence, REFUSE with a message that names each missing review and how to get it (run the scope sync or go --scope so the review is queued, or swarm tickets ID --review to queue it if such a command exists), and do not write anything; --force and --yes never bypass this review gate (they only confirm a legal transition); a ticket with recorded passing reviews, or one that needs none, can be set to done as before; a --dry-run shows the refusal reason without writing. Add tests to tests/scope-set-guard.test.mjs: a sensitive ticket without a security review cannot be set to done even with --force; with a recorded passing security review it can; a ticket needing an acceptance review without one is refused; a non-sensitive ticket is unchanged; the refusal writes nothing. Write only tools/scope-commands.mjs, tools/tickets.mjs, tests/scope-set-guard.test.mjs, and any existing test whose expectation this change must update.
